subject: Advance notice: third-party dataflow authorization & DPA implications
messages:
From: Natalie Burns <natalie.burns@mainsys.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: permission for onward transfer to ThirdWave Analytics

Hi Diego,

Hope youre well — quick question from our privacy team. Were onboarding ThirdWave Analytics to process aggregated usage telemetry for our product analytics. As part of that integration, MainSys will route a subset of anonymized request/usage metadata derived from calls to Redwoods hosted API to ThirdWave.

Before we proceed we need written confirmation from Redwood that:
- You permit this onward transfer (a narrow scope: telemetry + anonymized token counts, no PII or raw model outputs).
- Any contract language you require (DPA addendum / subprocessor clause) and a preferred contact for DocuSign.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II reporting or equivalent, and a completed SIG/CAIQ excerpt rather than running a full questionnaire.

Attached is ThirdWaves brief overview of data theyll receive. Can you point me to the right person and timeline? Our legal team would like confirmation within 72 hours if possible to keep the integration schedule.

Thanks,
Natalie Burns
Head of Privacy & Risk — MainSys Industries
Attachments: thirdwave-integration-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Burns <natalie.burns@mainsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: permission for onward transfer to ThirdWave Analytics

Natalie, thanks for the heads up and the clear scope. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Security / Vendor Risk) to review — leaving them to confirm contract language and evidence requirements.

My quick take: Redwood generally permits onward transfers that are narrowly scoped and documented, provided we have a DPA addendum or written consent and vendor risk evidence. We do require 30 days notice for new subprocessors in our standard procurement flow, but we can expedite reviews when its telemetry-only and theres no raw content involved.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm what we need to provide (DPA redline or signed addendum) and whether the provided scope (anonymized telemetry + token counts) meets our policy for expedited approval?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Natalie Burns <natalie.burns@mainsys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: permission for onward transfer to ThirdWave Analytics

Thanks for the loop. Natalie — appreciate the clear summary. I reviewed ThirdWaves summary you attached. To be explicit, Redwoods approvals for onward transfers require three items before we sign off: 

1) A signed DPA addendum or an explicit amendment to the existing DPA that lists ThirdWave as an onward transfer recipient and confirms theyll act only on MainSyss instructions. If youd like, we can propose a short addendum (I attached a proposed redline for your team).

2) Evidence of ThirdWaves security posture: SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent + completed SIG excerpt or CAIQ answers for the controls that map to data handling, encryption, incident response, and vendor access. We can accept a completed SIG Lite questionnaire; full SIG is not required for telemetry-only transfers.

3) A dataflow matrix describing exactly which attributes are transferred, retention windows, and access controls. Ive requested Karthiks team produce a short dataflow template; in the meantime please confirm whether any de-identification or hashing will be applied before transfer.

Operational notes: our policy requires 30 days notice from approval to production. Given the narrow scope, were comfortable issuing conditional approval within 3 business days if (a) DPA addendum is signed, (b) we receive SOC 2 or SIG Lite, and (c) the dataflow matrix limits transfer to aggregated/anonymized telemetry only.

Attaching: proposed DPA redline (dpa-redline-proposed.pdf) and guidance checklist.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: dpa-redline-proposed.pdf (pdf), subprocessor-checklist.txt (text)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Natalie Burns <natalie.burns@mainsys.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: permission for onward transfer to ThirdWave Analytics

Looping in a short technical confirmation. Natalie — I reviewed the attachment and the proposed scope. From a security and controls perspective were comfortable with a limited onward transfer provided the following technical mitigations are in place: 
- Pseudonymization/hashing of any identifiers prior to transfer (one-way hash with salt managed by MainSys).
- Token counts and telemetry aggregated at a session-level (no raw prompts or model outputs).
- TLS in transit, storage encrypted at rest by ThirdWave (AES-256 or equivalent).
- Role-based access controls and a documented retention policy (max 90 days unless business justification provided).

I also attached a short dataflow matrix our team completed for clarity (dataflow-matrix-v1.xlsx). If MainSys can confirm the hashing approach and sign the DPA addendum Marissa proposed, Redwood will provide conditional written permission to proceed and will target production enablement after the 30-day notice window or earlier if we finish the review and DocuSign.

For evidence: you can accept our SOC 2 Type II summary link (we shared in the support portal) and we will send a SIG Lite export (attached: sig-answers-2026.docx).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Vendor Risk
Redwood Inference
Attachments: dataflow-matrix-v1.xlsx (xlsx), sig-answers-2026.docx (docx)
